title: Pro-étale direct image along a universal homeomorphism is an equivalence (abelian-valued sheaves)
statement: Let $r\colon X\to Y$ be a universal homeomorphism of schemes [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism] and $\mathcal A$ a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Then the direct image $r_*\colon\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal A)$ between the categories of $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves on the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], given by restriction along the base change $V\mapsto V\times_YX$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], is an equivalence of categories.

source.place: i-topology: topological invariance of the topos used for D^b_ctf (sk-i-topology), here for A-valued pro-etale sheaves; Lean: upstream file lean/WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/ProEtale/FiniteCoefficient/UpperLowerStar/TopInvariance.lean, declaration AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isEquivalence_lowerStar_of_isUniversalHomeomorphism (module WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.FiniteCoefficient.UpperLowerStar.TopInvariance, lines 55-56, proof `sorry`)

proof.text: Work in the compatible small models and coefficient universe of the pro-etale site. Put $C=Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $D=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $u=u_r:C\to D$. Both sites have finite limits: the identity of $Y$ (resp. $X$) is a final object, and for maps $V_1\to V\leftarrow V_2$ of the site the fibre product $V_1\times_VV_2\to V_2$ is weakly etale by base change and its composite with $V_2\to Y$ is weakly etale by composition [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], so the chosen fibre product of the size convention is an object of the site and is the fibre product there. The inverse-image definition states that $u$ preserves the final object, fibre products and coverings; preservation of finite limits follows by constructing products as fibre products over the final object and equalizers as pullbacks of diagonals. The pro-etale subcanonicality lemma supplies that every representable on each site is a sheaf. Thus these are subcanonical sites and $u$ has exactly the continuity and finite-limit hypotheses of the coefficient-lifting lemma.

The existing set-valued topological-invariance theorem applies to the given universal homeomorphism $r$ without a finiteness or noetherian hypothesis. Its direct-image equivalence is precisely $R_{\mathrm{set}}(H)=H\circ u^{\mathrm{op}}$, by the direct-image formula. Separately, completeness of a Grothendieck abelian category gives all limits indexed by categories small in the coefficient universe. Here, as in the upstream declaration, whose $\mathcal A$ has its Hom sets and its Grothendieck structure in the universe of the set-valued sheaves, $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck relative to the coefficient universe $\mathcal V$ of the pro-etale site, so its Hom sets lie in that universe; hence $\mathcal A$ satisfies the locally small and complete hypotheses of the coefficient-lifting lemma. These limits include the small section-indexed diagrams, not limits over the whole category of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09AB, lemma-thickening; completeness supplied by Mathlib GrothendieckCategory/Basic.lean:102-104

proof.text: Apply the complete-valued sheaf equivalence-lifting lemma to $u$ and $\mathcal A$ using steps 1 and 2. It gives an equivalence for the actual restriction functor $R_{\mathcal A}$. For every $\mathcal A$-valued sheaf $G$ and object $V\to Y$ its value is $G(u(V))=G(V\times_YX)$, and on arrows and natural transformations it is the same precomposition. This is exactly the direct image $r_*$ specified in the statement, so that direct image is an equivalence.
